rv.q: Matilda is a fabulous family fizzer. It has strong tunes, witty lyrics and enough 'eew!' moments to satisfy the most revolting urchin.
It's hard to imagine a show capturing the spirit of Roald Dahl's literary world more perfectly than this one.
It's an evening of unadulterated bliss.
This generous, big-hearted piece is already being spoken of as one of the best new British musicals in years.
It is the best new British musical since Billy Elliot.
But the tremendous heart and intelligence of the piece remains undimmed.
Powerful, funny and beautifully musical, it reminds us who we are, and who we might be.
It is nothing of the sort. The best pieces of musical theatre come from great collaborations.
Matilda the Musical is nevertheless hugely enjoyable and cracking Christmas fun.
For kids, yes, but also for the children that we all remain at heart, this is wise, wicked, glorious fun.
But it’s still dark, daring and a lot of fun.
But there are a few bumps in the adaptation by Dennis Kelly, and Tim Minchin's songs are deficient in nothing except melody
This Matilda is a cunning combination of gross cartoon, pitch-perfect professionalism and endearing feel-good factor.

It proves an absolute cracker of a show, bursting with dynamism, fizzing with verve and packed full of slightly naughty children swung around by their pigtails played by incredible child actors who perform their socks off.
